subject: Renjin, Gradle, and Google App Engine

messages.author: 335ef9196fe8db4f
messages.subject: Renjin, Gradle, and Google App Engine
parts:
Hello,

I'm having some trouble getting the code in the documentation (http://docs.renjin.org/en/latest/introduction.html#setting-up-a-java-project-for-renjin) working. When I attempt to getEngineByName, on my local development server, the returned engine is null. However, the engine is returned correctly during my unit tests. I assumed that this because the Renjin jars are missing from my CLASSPATH on the dev server while being present for my jUnit tests. This does turn out to be the case when I print the CLASSPATH in both situations.

Is there something I'm missing to get the CLASSPATH to be populated correctly on the dev server? I'm using Gradle as my build system. This is how I'm declaring Renjin as a dependency:

repositories {
    maven { url "http://nexus.bedatadriven.com/content/groups/public/" }
}

...

dependencies {
    compile group: 'org.renjin', name: 'renjin-appengine', version:'0.7.0-RC8-SNAPSHOT'
}

Here is the sample of App Engine code that runs correctly but only in a jUnit test:

public RResponse runFunction(@Named("function") String function) {
    RResponse response = new RResponse();

    ScriptEngineManager manager = new ScriptEngineManager();
    ScriptEngine engine = manager.getEngineByName("Renjin");

    /* This is how I checked the CLASSPATH */
    System.out.println(System.getProperty("java.class.path"));

    try {
        engine.eval(function); /* NullPointerException is thrown here */
        response.setCode("SUCCESS");
    } catch (ScriptException e) {
        response.setCode("FAILURE");
        response.setReason(e.getMessage());
    }

    return response;
}

Is there something special that I need to do to get this working in a Google Cloud Endpoint API?

Thanks!
Ivan

messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: Renjin, Gradle, and Google App Engine
parts:
Hi Ivan,
You probably want to use a more recent release of Renjin, which is
perhaps confusingly, 0.7.1548, but other than that, your Gradle
configuration looks fine.

However, in order to run in the AppEngine environment, you will need
to create your ScriptEngine using the AppEngineContextFactory, which
helps you create a Session that is configured to be AppEngine-safe.
Otherwise the ScriptEngine initialization will fail silently when shot
down by the gae sandbox.

See the example here:
https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin-examples/blob/master/appengine-servlet/src/main/java/org/renjin/example/appengine/RenjinServlet.java

Does that help?
Alex
